subject: Intermittent checkout latency and 5xx spikes — suspected path jitter
messages:
From: Tim Erickson <tim@shopverse.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai; ops@shopverse.com
Cc: support@shopverse.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout latency + 502s — started 8:50 PST

Hey Aditya / Redwood team,

We started seeing intermittent latency and 502/504 spikes on the live checkout at ~08:50 PST. Impact is around 1–3% of checkout requests but it's spiking in short bursts (30–60s) every 10–15 minutes. Graphs attached. Our customers are seeing slow payments and some failed orders.

What we have observed: 
- Latency jumps from ~80ms P50 to 2–3s P50 during bursts
- 502 rate climbs from 0.1% to ~2% briefly
- All errors correlate with a handful of upstream timeouts to redwood-inference endpoints in us-west-2

We’re happy to share access to our dashboards — attached are Datadog slices and a quick curl trace. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (peering, config, rollout) around that time? We need a rapid mitigation plan — downgrading traffic if necessary.

Thanks,
Tim Erickson
Head of Platform
ShopVerse
attachments: datadog-graphs-20270503.png, curl-trace.txt

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Tim — thanks for the heads up and the graphs. We’re actively investigating.

Immediate items: 
1) I’ve looped in our on-call network lead (sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai) to look at VPC peering, route tables and any DNS anomalies.
2) Please keep the Datadog slices coming and, if possible, capture a tcpdump at ~10:00 PST window.
3) We’ll validate whether a model rollout or autoscaler event happened that could amplify tail latency.

I’ll coordinate a temporary traffic-routing plan if the root cause is on our egress path. For transparency, I’m CC’ing Rishi (account lead) and Evelyn (VP Customer Success). Expect a follow-up in ~30–45 minutes with initial findings and next actions.

—Aditya Rao

Redwood Inference

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, Tim Erickson <tim@shopverse.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout latency + 502s — suspected path jitter (investigation notes)

On Mon, May 3, 2027 at 09:28 AM aditya_rao@redwood.ai wrote:
> Tim — thanks for the heads up and the graphs. We’re actively investigating.

Team — quick notes from the infra side after a fast triage:
- No config change or rollout recorded in the model fleet around 08:30–09:00 PST.
- Control plane shows increased connection reset counts from a subset of us-west-2 frontend hosts to the edge egress cluster (egress-proxy-west-2-a).
- BGP telemetry indicates transient route re-advertisements between Redwood egress fabric and our peering partner in us-west-2 during the exact windows reported.
- DNS latencies from our edge to the resolver used by the ShopVerse route spiked (~150ms to 700ms) before the first 502 burst. We pulled resolver logs (attached vpc-route-export-20270503.txt).

Preliminary hypothesis: a combination of route flap in peering and elevated resolver latencies led to increased connection setup time and KV cache misses, producing tail latency and occasional 502s. Not seeing evidence of target overload yet.

Immediate mitigations we recommend: 
1) Failover to alternate peering (we have an idle path via us-west-1) for ShopVerse traffic — will require a short re-route (~90s) but should remove the jitter window.
2) Add persistent DNS caching on the affected frontends to reduce resolver sensitivity (quick patch).
3) If the ShopVerse team can send a tcpdump of one of the failing client traces we can correlate to the exact SYN/RST timing.

I will open a ticket with the peering provider and keep Rishi and Aditya posted. Attaching route export and a quick telemetry snapshot.

—Sergio Alvarez
Network Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
attachments: vpc-route-export-20270503.txt

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Tim Erickson <tim@shopverse.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout latency + 502s — action & executive summary

Tim — short executive update and next steps.

What happened (summary):
- Root cause: transient route re-advertisements on a primary us-west-2 peering link combined with elevated DNS resolver latency, causing repeated connection setup delays and KV cache misses on our frontends. Those events produced short bursts of high tail latency and a small increase in 502s during the windows you observed.

What we did: 
- Re-routed ShopVerse traffic to the alternate peering path (us-west-1) at 12:03 PST — elimination of latency bursts confirmed by both Redwood and ShopVerse charts.
- Deployed a short-term persistent DNS caching patch to frontends as an immediate mitigation.
- Opened a peering incident with our upstream provider; they acknowledged a flapping session and are doing a hardware swap.

Impact: 
- Peak error rate returned to baseline within 4–6 minutes after failover. No data loss and no model corruption.

Follow-ups and action items: 
- Sergio to publish a post-mortem with packet captures and BGP timelines (ETA 48 hours).
- Redwood to propose a more robust transit routing policy (BGP dampening + secondary resolver assignment) — we will share a proposed config and implementation timeline by Friday.
- Joint runbook update with ShopVerse for automated failover triggers (we can provide a sample webhook-driven reroute trigger).

Attachments: shopverse_maa_response.pdf (customer impact summary), datadog-graphs-20270503.png

We’re sorry for the disruption — I know short-lived spikes like this are still disruptive for ShopVerse during peak shopping. Rishi and I will be available for any executive sync you need with your leadership.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Cc: Evelyn Hart — VP, Customer Success (evelyn_hart@redwood.ai)
